identity.title: ALMA Multi-line Imaging of the Nearby Starburst NGC 253

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present spatially resolved ($\sim$50 pc) imaging of molecular gas species in the central kiloparsec of the nearby starburst galaxy NGC 253, based on observations taken with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).

evidence.quote: Throughout the paper we adopt a distance to NGC 253 of 3.5 Mpc (Rekola et al. 2005), i.e., 1$"$ corresponds to 17 pc at that distance.

question.value: What are the spatially resolved molecular line properties, chemistry, opacities and dense gas conditions across the central starburst of NGC 253 in the 3 mm band?

evidence.quote: The primary goal is to obtain spatially resolved views of the different molecular environments in and around the starburst center.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA #2011.0.00172.S.
A total of 50 molecular lines are detected over a 13 GHz bandwidth imaged in the 3 mm band.

analysis_steps.goal: Build line cubes and integrated intensity maps

method.value: Continuum-subtract, make per-line cubes, mask with CO(1-0), sum all data, primary-beam correct

evidence.quote: The integrated intensity map for a given line was then derived by simply adding all data in the respective data cube (without any further flux cutoff).

validation.value: Compared recovered flux with single-dish values (>=50%)

evidence.quote: it appears that the data consistently detect at least 50 % of their respective single dish fluxes

analysis_steps.goal: Measure line intensities at 10 regions and assign uncertainties

method.value: Peak integrated intensity from beam-matched maps; 10% error for S/N>10, 30% for 5<S/N<10, ignore S/N<5

evidence.quote: We thus adopt a conservative 10% error for pixels that have been detected at high $S$/$N$ ($>10$)

analysis_steps.goal: Derive excitation temperature, column densities and abundances

method.value: Optically thin LTE column densities; Tex from SO(32-21)/SO(22-11) ratio; N(H2) from CO(1-0) with XCO
